# Exercise 02

Suppose you estimate the following model by ordinary least squares:

$y_t = \alpha + \beta_0 x_t + \beta_1 x_{t-1} + \beta_2 x_{t-2} + u_t$

and obtain the following output.

**Coefficients**

| x | Estimate | Std. Error | t value | Pr(> |t|) |
| ---- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| (intercept) | 0.0011 | 0.0118 | 0.09 | 0.928 |
| x | 0.20 | 0.06 | 3.33 | 0.001 |
| x_l1 | 0.14 | 0.06 | 2.33 | 0.021 |
| x_l2 | 0.05 | 0.05 | 1.00 | 0.318 |

Assume the sample has $n = 300$ observations ( after accounting for lags) and that large-sample normal critical values can be used for t tests.
